title: A middle people
hook: We made you a community of the middle way (2:143)

segments.voice: Yesterday: Ya'qub's wasiyyah, and your line, what will you keep after me. Today, a word about a whole community.

Al-Baqarah has two hundred eighty-six verses. Divide by two, and you land on verse one hundred forty-three. Many readers have noticed that the verse in the middle of the longest surah is the verse about being in the middle. Whether that's design or coincidence, the Qur'an doesn't say, and scholars don't build anything on it. But it makes the verse easy to find, and it fits what the verse says. Today: wasat.
screen: `TWO HUNDRED EIGHTY-SIX, DIVIDED BY TWO.` → `VERSE ONE HUNDRED FORTY-THREE.` → `THE MIDDLE VERSE, ABOUT THE MIDDLE.`

segments.voice: Last year you met this verse in the story of the qiblah turning toward Mecca. This year, look at one word. In Pickthall's words: “Thus We have appointed you a middle nation.” The Arabic is ummatan wasatan. Wasat means the middle, the center, but in Arabic the middle is also the best part: the middle of the valley, where the water runs; the middle of the family, the most honored. A hadith in Bukhari explains the word in this very verse with one other: 'adl, just, balanced. The verse gives a reason: a middle people, so that you may be witnesses over humanity, and the messenger a witness over you. A witness has to stand where both sides can be seen; you can't see the whole field from one end zone. So what does the middle look like in a life? Bukhari tells of three men who asked about the Prophet's worship and found it less than they expected. One said: I'll pray all night, every night. Another: I'll fast every day. A third: I'll never marry. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ came to them and said, in effect: I'm the most mindful of God among you, and I fast and I eat, I pray and I sleep, and I marry. Whoever turns from my way is not of me. The middle isn't lukewarm. It's the balance that lets someone keep going for a lifetime, and see both sides clearly enough to be a fair witness.
screen: `UMMATAN WASATAN: A MIDDLE NATION` · `THE MIDDLE IS THE BEST PART` · `A WITNESS STANDS WHERE BOTH SIDES SHOW` · `I FAST AND I EAT, I PRAY AND I SLEEP`

segments.voice: Look for one place in your life that has drifted to an end: working every evening, scrolling past midnight, swearing off sugar forever, or doing nothing at all for something you care about. Picture its middle, not zero and not everything, the amount you could keep up for a year, and rest there for a few breaths.
Wasat. The middle: in Arabic, also the best and the most just. Al-Baqarah calls the Muslim community a middle nation, so it can be a fair witness. Today's word.
Your line: the middle way. In Arabic, the middle is also the best part. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Muslim scholars often cite 2:143 and the hadith of the three men in Bukhari when teaching moderation in worship: steady, sustainable practice rather than extremes of devotion or neglect.
